evidence: The user's answers in the local-order interview, 2026-10-24. (5) An answer that concludes 'no order' is refused until every applicable analysis has run: the existing list (analyze_modulations, a per-site directions map, analyze_clusters for every element whose own first shell is a finite cluster's), the diffuse verdict and polyhedral_distortion for extended networks. The diffuse verdict is analyze_modulations' own (plan item 4.4), so it adds no requirement. polyhedral_distortion: taken as every element that is no cluster element (the shell catalogue's own-kind rule, clusterElementsOf) and whose nearest closed first shell of another element holds an octahedron or a tetrahedron (CN 6 or 4 within the CN margin; networkCentresOf, POLYHEDRON_COUNTS), counted only where the turn offers the tool (it is not on main yet). On the Demo: Ga (GaSe4; Ta is a cluster element, its TaSe6 octahedra analyze_clusters reaches); on the dev perovskites the B site (TiO6, NbO6, TaO6), not the A site (twelve O) nor O (two B); both sites of the rock-salt and zincblende cases; none in the cluster cases. A judgment to confirm: isolated polyhedra (the Demo's GaSe4, which share no Se) are included, since no finite cluster holds them either and polyhedral_distortion reads isolated polyhedra too. Before: the gate's 'no order' row needed the existing list only, and promptGaps listed 'not polyhedral_distortion'. (6) Only antiphase or general-q diffuse order past the bar counts as order; in-phase correlation is reported as 'neighbouring cells moving together (correlated motion), not order' and never supports a 'no correlation' statement. The engine's verdict is unchanged (its answer is true past the bar in either phase); the reading is one predicate pair in the tool (isDiffuseOrder: correlated_antiphase; isCorrelatedMotion: correlated_in_phase), which the tool's facts (facts.modulation.diffuse, the passing verdicts with their phase) and arm A+ (SWEEP_RULES.diffuseOrder) share. analyze_modulations' in-phase note now reads '... neighbouring cells moving together (correlated motion; as RMC's long waves and acoustic-like thermal motion give), not order' (arm C: '(correlated motion), not order'; +8 characters on the Demo). Three checks on the answer: no-order ('no order' when an analyze_modulations of the question found order: an ordered zone-boundary point, an ordered general mode, or a diffuse verdict in antiphase; not when the sentence names order between cells or antiphase), correlated-motion (order between cells, short-range order, when none was found: in phase only, correlated motion, not order) and no-correlation (no correlation of displacements or cells when a correlation passed, in phase included). Known answers both ways: the modulation fixture's antiphase case (Nb, [1 0 0], -0.29 at 3.67 sigma) is order ('no order' flagged, 'short-range order' passes) and its in-phase case (Nb, [0 0 1], +0.47 at 4.6 sigma) is correlated motion ('short-range order' flagged, 'no order' passes, 'uncorrelated' flagged); the Demo's three elements pass the diffuse test in phase. Arm A+: a passing antiphase verdict maps to the modulation kind, the verdict's one kind for order between cells (FEATURE_KINDS), with no q; it scores without a change to scoring.js: a planted modulation with a q is found with its q undetermined (0.5), one not planted is spurious; it explains its element's split sites as an ordered point does. On the dev set no verdict or score moves: no dev case passes the diffuse test; every A+ record's analyze_modulations reading now adds the diffuse verdict (15 records, readings only). On the answer corpus the three checks raise no finding (no answer says no order, short-range order or uncorrelated after analyze_modulations ran). Approved by the user, 2026-10-24.
